# AeroGlobe: appendix {.page-title}

[Static data pipeline · snapshot notes]{.kicker}

These notes support the [AeroGlobe case study](../aeroglobe.qmd) and describe the 23 October 2026 snapshot. They are a scope record, not a live status page.

## Pipeline stages

| Stage | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normalize | OpenSky state vectors or adsb.lol day files | One record shape |
| Segment | Normalized observations | Per-aircraft tracks and flights |
| Chunk | Flights | Hourly JSON chunks with a size limit |
| Catalog | Chunks | The manifest the browser loads |

## Data sources

| Source | Use | Terms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenSky snapshots | A few real observations for the live demo | OpenSky terms; rate-limited |
| adsb.lol daily files | Full historical days, built on the owner's machine | ODbL, © adsb.lol contributors |
| Generated fixtures | Deterministic offline tests and the labeled sample day | Project code |

A full global day needs about 10 GB of disk and roughly 6 GB of RAM at build time.

## Built versus planned at the snapshot

| Built | Planned, not built |
| --- | --- |
| Globe client with search, filters and flight cards | A published real historical day |
| Playback, track replay and trails | Off-main-thread decoding and a transport bar |
| Static pipeline, catalog and hourly chunks | Inferred routes and a time-zone overlay |
| OpenSky snapshot and fixture commands | Per-aircraft history and a browser logbook |
| Reference airport, airline and time-zone tables | — |

## Snapshot counts

The case study lists 395 passing tests in 42 files, about 5,800 lines of TypeScript, and a clean lint, type-check and production build. Those are the 23 October 2026 figures; they are not a current passing-test total.

## Reproduce

```sh
npm install
DATA_SOURCE=fixtures npm run build     # offline, deterministic sample data
npm run build:check
```

The live deployment is built from the `gh-pages` branch; the repository documents the build-time snapshot fallback and the optional data branch.

:::
